key_insight: The paper presents a unified finite element framework that preserves geometric structure and energy dissipation for curve and surface flows with curvature-dependent and orientation-dependent bending energies.
engineering_relevance: It provides a reliable simulation tool for evolving interfaces in mechanics and materials where anisotropy, bending, and conservation of area or volume must be captured accurately.
method: Fully discrete parametric FEM for closed curves in 2D and closed surfaces in 3D
Couples geometric and curvature updates with a discrete energy inequality
Uses continuous piecewise linear elements, a surface energy matrix, and mass-lumped projection of curvature derivatives
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments report approximately second-order convergence in manifold distance and verify the expected discrete energy dissipation and area/volume conservation properties.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on positive densities and a directional convexity condition in curvature, so highly nonconvex or poorly resolved anisotropic energies may require careful implementation.
paper_title: A unified structure-preserving framework for geometric flows with coupled orientation and curvature dependence
